name: Dracut
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Dracut, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Dracut, MA: the Town Hall Holiday Drive-Thru with Frosties, Santa at Farmer Dave's, a Christmas art camp, and trains in Lowell.
lede: Dracut celebrates Christmas with a Holiday Drive-Thru at Town Hall, where families stay in the car to see lights, inflatables and the Frosties, plus farm and studio fun around town.
celebrates: Dracut's best known holiday event is the Holiday Drive-Thru at Town Hall on Arlington Street, run by the Town of Dracut with the Centralville Sportsmen's Club. Town Hall turns into a winter wonderland of festive lights, inflatable decorations and Christmas music, children get goodie bags, and families can look for the Frosties, which later move to spots around town. Santa's elves collect unwrapped presents for the Dracut Fire Department and Toys for Local Children. Farmer Dave's hosts breakfast with Santa, the Parker Memorial Library runs holiday programs, and Hammar's Studios on Lakeview Avenue holds a Christmas art camp.
lastyear: On Saturday, December 13, 2025, the Holiday Drive-Thru returned to Dracut Town Hall at 62 Arlington Street from 5 to 7 pm. Cars entered from either end of Fox Avenue, turned onto Chapman Street and then Lafayette Street to reach Town Hall, where lights, inflatables and Christmas music waited, along with goodie bags for children and elves collecting unwrapped toys for local kids.
facts: Dracut is pronounced DRAY-kut, and it is the only town in the world with that exact name and spelling. In October 1665 the land was sold to Captain John Evered, also known as Webb, whose family is linked to Draycot Foliat in Wiltshire, England. Early settlers paid taxes to Chelmsford across the Merrimack River, and Dracut became its own town on February 26, 1701.
trains: Dracut has no railroad station of its own, but it sits right across the Merrimack River from Lowell. The LRTA 10 bus connects Dracut to Lowell station on the MBTA Commuter Rail Lowell Line, where trains run to Boston for a holiday trip into the city. For a Christmas train ride through the lights, Edaville in Carver runs its holiday train, and the Boston Street Railway Association shares Boston streetcar history with older kids.

kidfact: There is no other town in the whole world called Dracut. At the Holiday Drive-Thru, look for the Frosties at Town Hall, then try to find them around town.
faq: When is the Dracut Holiday Drive-Thru?

The Town of Dracut and the Centralville Sportsmen's Club hold the Holiday Drive-Thru at Town Hall, 62 Arlington Street, on a Saturday evening in December. In 2025 it ran on December 13 from 5 to 7 pm. The town posts the date on its official online calendar each year.
How does the Dracut Holiday Drive-Thru work?

Families stay in their cars. In 2025 the town asked drivers to enter from either end of Fox Avenue, turn onto Chapman Street and then left onto Lafayette Street to reach Town Hall. Kids see lights, inflatables and the Frosties, get a goodie bag, and can hand an unwrapped toy to Santa's elves at the end.

The Frosties are part of the Holiday Drive-Thru. They appear at Town Hall during the event and are then moved to different places around Dracut, so families can drive around town afterward and try to find them. The town describes it as part of the holiday cheer that the Centralville Sportsmen's Club helps bring to Dracut.
Is there a train station in Dracut?

No. The closest MBTA Commuter Rail stop is Lowell station on the Lowell Line, just across the Merrimack River. The LRTA 10 bus runs between Dracut and Lowell station, and from there trains go to Boston for holiday outings in the city with kids.
